comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred tax asset valuation allowance policy
comparisons.peer_summary: A valuation allowance is recorded for deferred tax assets unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not; conversely, if realization is deemed more-likely-than-not, existing valuation allowances may be reversed, resulting in a credit to income tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose the specific use and exclusion of deferred tax valuation allowances as part of their segment reporting or financial adjustments. Intel explicitly excludes $9.9 billion in deferred tax valuation allowances from its segment results for decision-making purposes, whereas AMD discusses the general policy for recording valuation allowances when recovery of deferred tax assets is not more-likely-than-not. While Intel focuses on the exclusion for management reporting, AMD details the criteria for establishing such allowances.

sentences.text: Our segments' results of operations presented below exclude the $7.0 billion of restructuring and other charges and $9.9 billion of charges resulting from valuation allowances recorded against our net deferred tax assets, in addition to certain other items, as our CODMs receive, view, and use information for decision-making purposes based upon segment results that exclude such items.

Unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not (a probability level of more than 50%), we will record a charge to income tax expense in the form of a valuation allowance for the deferred tax assets that we estimate will not ultimately be recoverable or maintain the valuation allowance recorded in prior periods.

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom both disclose significant restructuring charges that are excluded from or highlighted in their segment/operating results. Intel excludes $7.0 billion in restructuring and other charges from segment results for CODM decision-making. Broadcom reports $1,533 million in restructuring charges primarily related to the VMware Merger. While Intel treats these as exclusions in segment reporting, Broadcom presents them as recognized operating expenses with specific drivers cited.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance for deferred tax assets
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, the company maintained valuation allowances of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards and certain state and other deferred tax assets determined not likely to be realized. If realization becomes more-likely-than-not, such deferred tax assets would be recognized as income tax benefits during the period.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both discuss deferred tax valuation allowances in the context of their financial results. Intel excludes $9.9 billion in charges resulting from valuation allowances against net deferred tax assets from its segment results. NVIDIA maintains a specific valuation allowance of $1.6 billion related to capital loss carryforwards and certain state deferred tax assets. Both companies recognize valuation allowances as significant items impacting their financial position, though Intel highlights the exclusion from segment metrics while NVIDIA reports the specific balance.

sentences.text: Our segments' results of operations presented below exclude the $7.0 billion of restructuring and other charges and $9.9 billion of charges resulting from valuation allowances recorded against our net deferred tax assets, in addition to certain other items, as our CODMs receive, view, and use information for decision-making purposes based upon segment results that exclude such items.

As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, we had a valuation allowance of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards, and certain state and other deferred tax assets that management determined are not likely to be realized due, in part, to jurisdictional projections of future taxable income, including capital gains.
